Lines.Text: BANG—!!
The heavy steel door burst open with an explosive crash.
Not a trace of warmth existed in the stark monochrome room.
Razor-straight chairs stood in formation around an enormous obsidian table,
while cold white light ran down the gray walls like the blade of a guillotine.

At the head of that suffocating fortress sat Kang Joo-hee, legs crossed, wearing the Chief Producer badge she had taken from P that very day. To her right, the hot-tempered Executive Kim smoked a cigarette. To her left, Executive Choi held a teacup.
To her right sat the hot-tempered Executive Kim, cigarette in hand; to her left, Executive Choi with a teacup.
P stormed in with his tie undone, panting like a cornered animal. Joo-hee flicked a tablet across the table toward him.
Try knocking. How vulgar.
(slamming both hands on the table) Kang Joo-hee. Killing their debut one week before launch wasn't enough,
so now you're billing them 480 million won in damages? And that sponsor rumor making the rounds—you planted it, didn't you?
Lower your voice. This is a factory. We assemble calibrated dolls and sell them.
I can't put defective units reeking of you into my first launch as Chief Producer.
Pulling them off the line and swapping in replacements is standard procedure.
Defective units?! You were the ones who dumped those girls on me when I was trapped in the past and could barely breathe!
I spent three years training them until their toenails fell off, and now you want to scrap them?!
Executive Choi set down his teacup and spoke in a gentle, kindly voice.
P, you seem to be laboring under a serious misunderstanding.
Three years ago, after that unfortunate rooftop incident left you broken, we gave you those girls as a kind of... rehabilitation toy.
...What?
S-Tier needs a genius producer like you. Letting you play at make-believe before the wound festered was an act of consideration.
Now that you've made such a fine recovery, surely it's only proper to put away a toy that has served its purpose.
His tone was the most polished and gracious in the room. His words were the most monstrous.
The realization that the girls had been used as toys for his recovery, then discarded, bleached P's mind blank.
(grinding out his cigarette in the ashtray) Listen, P. Even the chairman admits you've got talent. That's the only reason we've put up with this much.
So do what you did last time: shut your mouth and look the other way. Those bitches refused to pour drinks for the investors at that private dinner a few nights ago and ruined the whole mood anyway.
You sick fucking monsters...
(leaning forward to sneer at P) What? Scared these girls will drown in debt and jump off a roof too?
If they end up splattered on the pavement like the last one, cleanup and burying the story both cost money. Keep a tighter leash on them.
THUD.
The pale face of P's first idol, throwing herself from a rooftop years ago, crashed across his vision. His breath seized in his throat.
His nails dug into his palms until they drew blood. But before the violence of capital, fused into something as hard as obsidian, every scream was powerless.
WHIRRR—
He fled downstairs as if escaping hell. In the stark white basement, the only sound was the heavy drone of an air purifier that allowed not even a speck of dust.
Cold white LEDs poured down like the lights of a butcher's display case.
On the immaculate wood floor lay an obscene document: [Notice of Contract Termination and Claim for Damages].
Jiwoo sat collapsed against the mirrored wall. With a trembling hand, she held the notice and stared up at the dazed P.
P... is this real? Four hundred eighty million won...
The deposit on my mom's tteokbokki shop is only thirty million. We didn't do anything except sing and dance. How did this happen to us...?
(covering her ears, words spilling out in panic) The rumors are everywhere... They say we sell ourselves to sponsors behind the scenes.
All we've done is train ourselves half to death in this basement for three years... Why is everyone calling us trash...? Sniff...
Mina, so proud and fastidious it bordered on obsession, had forgotten even the dust clinging to her clothes. She stared into empty space, her eyes unfocused.
(laughing hollowly) It's over. If S-Tier went out of its way to bury us, who's going to pick damaged goods out of the garbage?
Three years of barely hanging on... tossed straight into the trash.
(trying to smile through tears that will not stop) Mina, don't. P went upstairs. He'll find some way to—
(screaming) How the hell is he supposed to fix this?!
The executives rigged the whole thing! What's one producer supposed to do against that kind of debt? How is he supposed to save us?!
Mina's scream tore through the empty practice room.
Ria, her face drained of color, pinched her thigh until it bled as she pulled the girls into her arms.
Enough... I'm the leader. I'll go to Producer Joo-hee and get on my knees if I have to.
I'll do anything she says. I'll beg her to spare us just this once. Please...
The girls had been used as someone's rehabilitation toys, then broken beyond repair.
Like shipwreck survivors, they crawled across the floor and clutched the hems of P's trousers as if they were a lifeline.
(gripping so hard the blood drains from her fingers) P... We didn't do anything.
Just because we wouldn't play nice in that private room... because we refused to act like their dolls... how does that become a 400-million-won death sentence?
(wrapping both arms around P's leg, sobbing) Please save us, P... How am I supposed to face my mom with this kind of debt?
(pleading through a face soaked with tears) We can't end like this. Please let us stand on the stage you spent three years shaping us for. Just once. Please...
(What? Scared they'll jump off a roof like the last one? Look the other way.)
Executive Kim's metallic voice became an auditory hallucination, stabbing into P's eardrums.
The girls hung from him and wailed like lambs trapped in a slaughterhouse. Looking down at them, P bit his split lip as though his heart were collapsing inside his chest.
Their desperate gazes had nowhere left to go.
Hot tears fell without end onto his worn shoes.
